name: Cat Riker
title: Honky Tonk Heroes & Pool Memories
body:
I've had the honor to call Pauly a friend since September 25, 2016 when I joined the Nick-A-Nees 9-Ball Pool team, Honky Tonk Heroes, he had joined the session before. That first night of the session was Honky Tonk Heroes vs. Nick-A-Nees. Home team vs. home team was always a coveted night because the room was full of all of our people, I miss those days! It was a close match but we lost 47-53, but gained friendship!

Upon our first introduction I learned he was a super cool Providence DJ and then I immediately learned that he was a devoted family man. It was so refreshing to know a guy my age who was totally devoted to his partner, family, and friends. We discovered we were both Edgewood kids with dozens of connections! I wished I had gone to Cranston East after leaning that. It was obvious that if I had met Pauly earlier, we would have been friends immediately because that's who he was- he was truly kind to EVERYONE. In true Rhode Island fashion, despite us not knowing each other, our childhoods intersected. My family would visit his families bakery every time my mom went for a haircut next door. We'd later learn that unbeknownst to us, my dad and his mom had been friends for years!

Paul was a great teammate and pool player. Despite Pauly having a busy successful DJ'ing Career he would make it to play with us pretty much every Sunday night. Honky Tonk Heroes began playing in 2011 and the team had different iterations over years but the core members when Paul joined in Summer of 2016 were Stephanie, Jim, Dina, Noah & Liz. Over the years Paul and I had many conversations about our admiration for those 5 humans, as well as, the other Nick-A-Nees folks that we had each added to our chosen extended families, especially fellow Honky Tonk Heroes: Scott, David, Tara, Matt, Vanessa & Damien.

On June 4, 2017 he and I both experienced our first high level pool tournament. I literally couldn't tell you the specifics of what happened that day, I know we lost, I'm sure it was stressful, but I bet we had fun. That day I began a tradition of taking an obligatory photo of the pond behind the pool venue. I've taken so many photos in that spot since that date and now they're all for Pauly.

In Fall of 2019 when Steff, Jim & Dina decided they were going to take a session off Pauly was kind enough to join my rag tag group of players. We were NOT the "cool kids", we were all inexperienced in the scheme of APA, but he loved us, so he stayed. That session our team took 1st place and Paul had an amazing session with a 67% win percentage! If Covid hadn't gone and ruined everything maybe I could have convinced him to stay playing with us. But I love and respect his decision to keep his family safe- see he was devoted family man 1st and foremost!

In 2023 Pauly started playing pool again with the other cool kids (I'd be lying if I told you I wasn't jealous to not be back with them all!) Those teammates can talk about how fantastic he was during those years- the raw data shows he was a rock star, his stats only faltered during one session, as he was adjusting to his newly earned higher rank.

Despite no longer playing on a team together we reminded friends, I mean duh, because Paul never stopped being someone's friend. I'm going to miss:
- Seeing him pop in to Nick-A-Nees for last call, and hopefully a quick game, on his way home from a gig.
- Rides home to Edgewood in the Volvo where he'd share updates on family and recent/upcoming gigs.
- Him DJ'ing the Nick-A-Nees Employee Party- I mean what a genius, I'm pretty sure Steff paid him to be there, but I KNOW he would have paid to do that gig!
- Him rolling into Jim & Dina's annual party with his homemade hummus.
- Seeing our friend's faces light up with joy as they chatted with him on endless topics!

Paul will be greatly missed and fondly remembered. have to end by stealing a quote from the GoFundMe page. I 100% agree that Paul "never missed a chance to stand by others, whether making the rounds at local venues and bars or showing up in times of celebration and grief."
